title: Micro-pacing prefetch scheduler for interleaved short/long contexts
creator: Aisha Romero
description: Background: Production traffic contains a high proportion of interleaved short prompts (user queries) followed by long responses (multi-paragraph generations) or vice-versa when agents call external tools. Our current continuous coalescing scheduler groups requests primarily by arrival window and length bins which reduces throughput for mixed-turn sessions and increases KV cache churn and GPU memory fragmentation. Problem: Tail latency spikes during bursts of interleaved short/long contexts and suboptimal KV residency (cold misses) for long responses lead to higher token cost and occasional OOMs on memory-constrained GPU slabs. Goals: 1) Reduce p95 inference latency tail for mixed-turn sessions by at least 15% under production traces. 2) Improve KV hit-rate for follow-on responses by keeping relevant prefixes resident without over-reserving slab memory. 3) Reduce observed GPU memory fragmentation (measured as unused slab bytes) by 20% for 8/16GB GPUs. Proposed approach: Implement a micro-pacing prefetch scheduler that augments the continuous batcher with three capabilities: 1) Admission micro-pacing: short-turn requests that are likely to be followed by long responses (inferred from prompt metadata / heuristics) are admitted into a reserved micro-window to ensure they can be coalesced with their subsequent continuation while not blocking large-batch throughput. 2) Windowed KV prefetch: when admission heuristics indicate a follow-on longer generation is probable, schedule a lightweight KV prefetch of the request prefix onto a soft-reserved slab region with an age-based eviction watermark. Prefetches are approximate (partial KV) to limit memory. 3) Slab-aware packing and soft preemption: the scheduler uses current slab occupancy maps to choose coalescing targets; if prefetch pressure would exceed slab safety, the scheduler soft-preempts lower-priority background batches and signals reduced prefetch depth. Design details: - Heuristics: simple logistic model using prompt length, user-agent tag, recent-turn timing, and presence of tool-call tokens. Model runs inline in scheduler with a tiny binary (latency <100us). - Micro-window size: tunable between 2-15ms, defaults to 8ms for mixed workloads. - Prefetch granularity: 25-50% of KV depth (configurable by model class). - Age watermark: prefetched KV has TTL in slots; evicted by LRU + age threshold. - Safety knobs: slab-reservation ceiling per GPU, global prefetch budget, adaptive backoff based on KV miss rate and OOM signals. Trade-offs considered: - Memory overhead vs. latency: prefetch improves follow-on latency at cost of some reserved memory; we limit this via partial KV and adaptive backoff. - Scheduling complexity vs. stability: we keep heuristics simple to avoid oscillation; heavier ML-based predictors deferred to follow-up. Success metrics: - p50/p95 token latency improvements on mixed-turn trace (target p95 -15%). - KV prefix hit rate increase for follow-up generations (+12% target). - GPU slab free bytes reduction by 20% variance in fragmentation metric. - Overall throughput equal or improved (+3% target) when measured at SLO headroom. Testing plan: 1) Offline trace-replay: run 72-hour production-sampled traces in the simulator (existing harness) with and without micro-pacing; measure latency, KV hit rate, slab fragmentation. 2) Microbench: run isolated workload mixes (short-heavy, long-heavy, interleaved) on 4 GPU types (A100-80GB, A100-40GB, H100-80GB, RTX6000-48GB) to validate slab behavior. 3) Stress tests: force-heavy concurrent openings to validate soft-preemption and no-OOM guarantee. 4) Canary rollout: staged enable via feature-flag: 0.5% -> 5% -> 20% -> 100% per cluster with rollback gates. Rollout and monitoring: - Start with a small fleet in eu-west with nightly ramp schedule. - Dashboards: p50/p95 latency per route, KV hit-rate, slab occupancy heatmap, OOM counts, scheduler decisions-per-second. - Alerts: p95 increase >5% vs baseline, OOM >1/day on canary nodes, KV miss-rate regression >7%. Acceptance criteria for GA: - Stable or improved latency and throughput at 20% canary. - No OOMs attributable to prefetch logic during a 48h canary window. - Dashboard telemetry annotated and runbook updated. Implementation milestones: 1) Scheduler prototype (Rust) and feature flag (2 weeks). 2) KV prefetch controller and slab accounting (2 weeks). 3) Heuristic model embedding and tests (1 week). 4) Benchmarks and canary (2 weeks). 5) Iteration and GA (1-2 weeks). Post-GA follow-ups: - Evaluate a learned predictor for follow-on generations. - Explore model-specific prefetch profiles and longer TTL options for stable sessions. - Integrate with cost-aware optimizer to weigh token cost against latency for prefetch decisions.
